weekly.title: ‘Cats Love Gravy’: How a Reporter Ended Up at a Pet Food Research Center
weekly.summary: A Times journalist and animal lover spent a day at a Royal Canin facility to understand how pet food giants are studying the taste buds of dogs and cats.

weekly.title: Arms Race Intensifies in Korea as the North Is Emboldened by Russia Alliance
weekly.summary: A rare escalation this month exposed the increasingly lethal arsenals the two Koreas are building up across the world’s most heavily fortified border.

weekly.title: A Cancer Revolution
weekly.summary: We look at how screening and groundbreaking treatments have radically reduced death rates.

weekly.title: How Pastors Mobilize Communities in Congo’s Fight Against Ebola
weekly.summary: As health care workers fought to control the latest outbreak this year, they got crucial aid from churches in beating back fear and misinformation.

weekly.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
weekly.summary: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.

weekly.title: Above Iran’s Capital, a Trump Impersonator Dances in a Jail Cell
weekly.summary: The Islamic republic has long used billboards in Tehran to mock its opponents and hammer home its messaging, but this piece of performance propaganda is perhaps the most eccentric yet.

weekly.title: Stocks See Steepest Decline in Months Amid A.I. Worries
weekly.summary: The S&P 500 index fell over 1.4 percent, its largest daily decline since July, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq slumped nearly 2.5 percent, that index’s biggest one-day decline since June.

weekly.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
weekly.summary: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.

weekly.title: Mortgage Rates Remain Above 7%, Pushing Home Prices Lower in Some Areas
weekly.summary: The 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped slightly to 7.32 percent as prospective home buyers continue to struggle with affordability. But home prices are starting to drop in some areas.

weekly.title: Employers Shift Rising Health Care Costs Onto Millions of Workers
weekly.summary: New surveys show that increases in premiums and deductibles are forcing people to forgo treatments or doctor’s visits while budgets are strained by higher food and gas prices.

weekly.title: Why Many Voters Are Unhappy With the Economy
weekly.summary: With the midterms approaching, the economy is a top concern for voters. Our chief economic correspondent, Ben Casselman, describes which aspects of the economy have voters so frustrated.

weekly.title: A.I. and Its Dangers Are Embedded In the Midterm Elections
weekly.summary: The midterms are the first elections in which artificial intelligence is integrated into every major social media platform. Efforts to blunt its harms are uneven.

weekly.title: France's Macron blames protests on 'ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic'
weekly.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron blamed "ultra-left groups" for riots and looting as Paris businesses board up windows ahead of Saturday protests.

weekly.title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
weekly.summary: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.

weekly.title: When Do Rules on Historic Preservation Go Too Far?
weekly.summary: Saratoga Springs, N.Y., stands out for its preservation efforts. But some say strict designs have become a burden for residents.

weekly.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
weekly.summary: Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.

weekly.title: Barclays to Cut 5,000 Jobs in A.I.-Driven Push to Lower Costs
weekly.summary: The move is the latest illustration of a company saying it believes it can be more efficient with fewer workers because of artificial intelligence.

weekly.title: Zuckerberg’s Big Deal to Stay in California
weekly.summary: The agreement that Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, cut to stay in California underscores businesses’ fears about a major tax proposal.

weekly.title: Macron has one more chance to save the country or ‘it’s lost for France,’ business owner warns
weekly.summary: A French business owner who had five family stores destroyed by looters warns of growing insecurity and urges authorities to protect businesses ahead of another weekend of protests.

weekly.title: Iowa, Usually Red, Is in Play This Midterm as Economic Woes Mount
weekly.summary: The Trump administration’s policies could cost Republicans in a state that is being hit hard by expensive diesel prices and uncertainty over trade.

weekly.title: Looted Goods From French Stores Appear on Resale Sites After Riots
weekly.summary: Officials in France are pressing online platforms like eBay and Vinted to remove items that were stolen during public disturbances over the weekend.

weekly.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
weekly.summary: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.

weekly.title: Tesla Profit Slumps as Elon Musk’s Car Company Considers Merging With SpaceX
weekly.summary: The carmaker, which is controlled by Elon Musk and is considering merging with another of his companies, SpaceX, spent heavily on artificial intelligence and other new technologies.

weekly.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion Over Cambridge Analytica Privacy Violations
weekly.summary: The penalty, one of the largest levied against a tech giant, stemmed from a lawsuit by New Mexico claiming the social media company had misled users about their data privacy.

weekly.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
weekly.summary: The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.

weekly.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
weekly.summary: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.

weekly.title: France Riots Expose the Rage Aimed at Dior, Hermès and Other Luxury Brands
weekly.summary: The looting of stores belonging to brands like Dior, Celine and Hermès has exposed a crack in the glossy facade.

weekly.title: U.S. to Tap Heating Oil Reserves Ahead of Midterm Elections
weekly.summary: The Trump administration will release 315,000 barrels of heating oil, but analysts say the amount is too small to make much of a difference.

weekly.title: Pope Leo XIV needs no further cancer treatment after lung tumor removed, doctors say
weekly.summary: Pope Leo XIV's doctors say the lung adenocarcinoma tumor removed Oct. 13 was localized, and a cancer assessment found no further treatment needed.

weekly.title: A.I. Discovered a Critical Vulnerability in PHP, a Coding Language Behind Many Websites
weekly.summary: The disclosure heightened concerns about A.I.’s potential to upend cybersecurity unless shortcomings are addressed.

weekly.title: Bibas family relative takes fight to ICC after mother, two young boys murdered by Hamas
weekly.summary: A relative of murdered mother Shiri Bibas and her sons Kfir and Ariel is pressing the ICC to act against Iranian leaders after the family’s devastating losses in the Oct. 7 attacks.

weekly.title: GM Aims to Bring ‘Eyes-Off’ Driving to AI-Powered Cars Within 2 Years
weekly.summary: General Motors is seeking help from artificial intelligence to keep up with Chinese companies that introduce vehicles very quickly.

weekly.title: Alaska’s Journalists Join Forces to Cover the Midterms
weekly.summary: The state’s challenging geography and newspapers’ broader economic struggles have stretched reporters in Alaska, just as its competitive U.S. Senate race has grabbed national attention.

weekly.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy open to freezing front lines in ceasefire with Russia
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he's open to freezing the front lines of the Ukraine-Russia war as a real path to end the conflict.

weekly.title: How The New York Times Reports on A.I. Images
weekly.summary: A Times reporter and editors discuss the challenges of sifting through what’s real and what’s not in pursuit of the news.

weekly.title: UK to Headphone Dodgers on Trains: Shush
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a campaign against listening to music or videos without headphones on public transportation. We asked London commuters to weigh in.

weekly.title: Russia releases American teacher imprisoned on Ukraine mercenary charges after Trump pressed Putin
weekly.summary: American Stephen Hubbard has been released from Russian custody after Trump urged Putin to free the retired teacher imprisoned on Ukraine mercenary charges.

weekly.title: China Criticizes U.S. Ban on DeepSeek A.I. in Government Systems
weekly.summary: The response came after Homeland Security ordered the removal and exclusion of products developed by the Chinese company.

weekly.title: Netflix Is Great at Making Money. Its Problem Is Keeping Viewers Hooked.
weekly.summary: The streaming service reported a 12 percent increase in quarterly revenue, but acknowledged that stagnant viewership, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, was a major concern.

weekly.title: SpaceX Swings to a Profit, as A.I. Business Grows
weekly.summary: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its artificial intelligence spending had soared, but revenue more than doubled from its Starlink internet satellite service and A.I. products.

weekly.title: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval
weekly.summary: After years of delay, the Federal Aviation Administration certified the 737 Max 10, the largest version of Boeing’s most popular plane.

weekly.title: Reporter's Notebook: France braces for more unrest after parts of Paris spun out of control
weekly.summary: French Prime Minister Lecornu says a massive police operation backed by the military will counter the next protest set for this weekend in France.

weekly.title: Sea mine crisis re-emerges in Strait of Hormuz as Tehran urges Washington to accept deal
weekly.summary: Iran claims two oil tankers struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz as the IMO warns the critical shipping lane remains too unsafe to transit.

weekly.title: Joel Kaplan, Meta’s Global Policy Chief, to Leave After 15 Years
weekly.summary: Joel Kaplan, a former adviser to George W. Bush known for his Republican ties, had helped Meta build its relationship with the Trump administration.

weekly.title: Google Reports Cloud Disruptions in Europe
weekly.summary: The disruptions began around 7 a.m. in London after what the tech giant called a “power event.”

weekly.title: Iran regime under pressure as rebel groups escalate attacks in volatile southeast
weekly.summary: A coalition of armed rebel groups is stepping up attacks against Iranian regime forces in the country's volatile southeast, raising questions about Tehran's grip on the region.

weekly.title: Saudis Aided Family of Engineer Accused of Bugging OpenAI, Prosecutors Say
weekly.summary: Saudi officials paid for his wife and son to fly out of the U.S. and offered to cover his bail, according to court filings. A judge ordered the engineer to remain in custody.

weekly.title: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
weekly.summary: Anthropic, an A.I. rival to SpaceX, earlier said it would form a “public benefit fund” and other tech moguls have contributed to savings accounts for children.

developing.title: No Kings turns its focus to voting this weekend. Here's what we know
developing.summary: The coalition behind nationwide anti-Trump protests is shifting its strategies this weekend to focus on voter turnout. Organizers say Saturday's events are a nonpartisan effort to get people to the polls.

developing.title: Live Updates: Protesters March in France Amid Heavy Security
developing.summary: In Marseille, clashes broke out between protesters and the police, who fired tear gas. As many as 70,000 police and security officers will try to avert the arson and looting that shocked the country last weekend.
